extracted.intended_audience: attorneys and other practitioners who practice before the USPTO; OED/disciplinary stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Standards, procedures, and factors used by the USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline (OED) to evaluate practitioner misconduct and impose discipline, including reporting obligations, reliance on state-bar dispositions, and sanctions. The document is a Final Order approving a settlement and describing the factual basis, legal conclusions, and sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.101–11.901)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent, practicing before the Office in trademark matters, is subject to the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct set forth at 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.101 through 11.901.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This establishes that practitioners appearing before the USPTO must follow the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct; the Final Order treats violations of these rules as grounds for discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO jurisdiction for disciplinary proceedings (35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D), 32; 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.19, 11.20, 11.26)
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over practitioner discipline pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and implementing regulations 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.19, 11.20, and 11.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These statutes/regulations define when the USPTO may initiate and resolve disciplinary actions against practitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-reporting obligation (37 C.F.R. § 11.24(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners are required to report certain events (including state disciplinary actions) to the USPTO under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(a); the Respondent did not report his Texas sanction as required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to timely self-report state discipline to the USPTO is itself a violation considered by OED; practitioners should disclose state disciplinary actions per the regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discipline predicated on being publicly disciplined by a state (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: Being publicly disciplined on professional misconduct grounds by a duly constituted state authority constitutes a violation under 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h); the Respondent acknowledged violating § 11.804(h) based on the Texas order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A state bar's public discipline can serve as an independent basis for USPTO discipline under the cited rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Texas Disciplinary Rule 1.01(b)(1) — Diligence
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigatory Panel 8-2 concluded Respondent violated Texas Disciplinary Rule 1.01(b)(1) (diligence) based on facts such as failing to respond to a No-Evidence Motion for Summary Judgment and mishandling hearings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples on this record: not timely responding to opposing motions and failing to protect client interests in litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Texas Disciplinary Rule 1.02(a)(2) — Scope of representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigatory Panel 8-2 concluded Respondent violated Texas Disciplinary Rule 1.02(a)(2) (scope of representation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The panel's findings include actions outside a client's consent (e.g., settling a client's claim without consent), illustrating scope-of-representation violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Texas Disciplinary Rule 1.03(a)-(b) — Communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigatory Panel 8-2 concluded Respondent violated Texas Disciplinary Rule 1.03(a)-(b) (communication), e.g., failing to notify the client or new counsel of an upcoming hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lack of communication with clients or their counsel about critical developments (hearings, settlements) supports a communication-rule violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Texas Disciplinary Rule 1.06(b)(1)-(2) — Conflict of interest (simultaneous representation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigatory Panel 8-2 concluded Respondent violated Texas Disciplinary Rule 1.06(b)(1)-(2) concerning conflicts of interest when he represented both Complainant and Client 2 without appropriate waivers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Representing multiple clients with potentially adverse interests without informed consent or waivers constitutes a conflict-of-interest violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Texas Disciplinary Rule 1.06(e) — Withdrawal from conflicts
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigatory Panel 8-2 concluded Respondent violated Texas Disciplinary Rule 1.06(e) regarding withdrawal from conflicts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Improper handling of withdrawal from representation where conflicts exist (or failing to take appropriate steps when withdrawing) is actionable under this rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Texas Disciplinary Rule 1.08(d) — Prohibited transactions
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigatory Panel 8-2 concluded Respondent violated Texas Disciplinary Rule 1.08(d) (prohibited transactions), tied to settlements and transactions lacking client consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settling a client's claim without the client's consent or engaging in transactions prohibited by the rules can constitute misconduct under this provision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliance on state-bar findings as evidentiary basis
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO OED accepted and relied upon the agreed facts and the Texas Agreed Judgment (probated suspension and findings) as the factual and legal basis for USPTO discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A practitioner’s negotiated state-bar disposition and factual findings may be adopted by OED in USPTO disciplinary proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors considered in determining sanction (mitigating and aggravating considerations)
rubrics_metrics.description: OED considered Respondent's representations that he did not adequately understand self-reporting obligations, his expressed contrition, that he had never been subject to USPTO discipline, his full cooperation with the OED investigation, and his compliance with the terms of the probated suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cooperation, candor, lack of prior USPTO discipline, contrition, and compliance with other imposed sanctions are mitigating factors that may influence the form and severity of discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of discipline — Reprimand
rubrics_metrics.description: As an agreed-upon sanction, Respondent is reprimanded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reprimand is an available sanction and in this case was the agreed remedy given the circumstances and considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Final Order (OED FOIA Reading Room) as disciplinary consequence
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order at the OED's electronic FOIA Reading Room (https://foiadocuments.uspto.gov/oed/).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public posting of disciplinary orders is part of the sanction scheme and provides notice to the public and to future adjudicators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Notice in the Official Gazette (content consistency requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: OED shall publish a notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the specified Notice of Reprimand, summarizing the conduct and state-bar findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Official Gazette notice must describe the practitioner's name, residence, rule violated, and the salient facts and findings that support the discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of disciplinary record in future proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the Final Order prevents the Office from considering this disciplinary record in (1) addressing further complaints of the same or similar misconduct, or (2) in future disciplinary proceedings against Respondent as an aggravating factor or to rebut statements by Respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior disciplinary records can be used to increase sanctions or rebut claims in later matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of procedural rights in settlement
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent waived rights to seek reconsideration under 37 C.F.R. § 11.56, waived review under 37 C.F.R. § 11.57, and waived other rights to appeal or challenge the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement agreements may include express waivers of procedural or appellate rights as part of resolving disciplinary matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs
rubrics_metrics.description: The parties shall bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of the Agreement and this Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The settlement specified that each party is responsible for its own costs; practitioners should be aware settlements may allocate costs explicitly.
